instruction: I have visual impairment and need better contrast to see the screen clearly. Can you enable high contrast mode to make interface elements more distinguishable?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: CONTRAST_MODE=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme 2>/dev/null); if echo "$CONTRAST_MODE" | grep -i "high-contrast\|highcontrast\|contrast" > /dev/null; then echo "High contrast theme enabled: $CONTRAST_MODE"; else echo "Standard theme in use"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling high contrast theme via Settings > Accessibility. Evaluator checks gsettings gtk-theme for high-contrast theme name. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks GTK theme setting via gsettings, which is the proper method to verify high contrast mode on Ubuntu/GNOME
Command logic is sound: executes gsettings query, uses grep to detect high-contrast theme keywords, outputs clear success/failure messages
Metric (check_include_exclude) correctly verifies the presence of success message and absence of failure messages
Complete coverage: instruction asks to enable high contrast mode, evaluator verifies if high-contrast theme is enabled
Good error handling: includes timeout (10s), stderr redirection, and checks for 'error' in exclude list
State is persistent (system setting), so no postconfig needed - can verify directly
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The grep pattern 'high-contrast|highcontrast|contrast' might match non-high-contrast themes that contain the word 'contrast' (e.g., 'low-contrast'). Consider using a more specific pattern like 'high-contrast|highcontrast|HighContrast' to avoid false positives, though this is unlikely to cause issues in practice since standard Ubuntu themes don't typically include 'contrast' in their names
